# Derivation 3.3A — Carrier-map source postulate and consequences {#sec-derivation-03-03A-carrier-source-map .unnumbered}

## Purpose

This appendix states the source identification used by the stationary M1
gravity construction and derives what follows from it without importing an
interacting source ledger.

## Role, regime, and status

- **Role:** selected source postulate followed by exact algebraic consequences.
- **Regime:** the counting is kinematic; its present gravitational use is weak
  and stationary.
- **Status:** the free-carrier map is explicit. Its microscopic origin and its
  extension through binding, walls, and interactions remain open.
- **Non-claim:** the postulate is not derived from Foundations, and the algebra
  below is not a complete theory of composite gravitating matter.

## Source identification

For a carrier with core-momentum magnitude

$$
M=\sqrt{p_f^2+\delta^{ij}p_i p_j},
$$

the opposed shell readings along an oriented axis $\hat k$ are

$$
p_k^+=M+\frac12p_k,
\qquad
p_k^-=M-\frac12p_k.
$$

The source identification (SI) postulates that gravity reads the local
densities of these quantities:

$$
\mathcal J_k^\pm(x)
=
\left\langle\sum_a
\left(M_a\pm\frac12p_{k,a}\right)\right\rangle_x .
\tag{3.3A.1}
$$

Here $\langle\cdot\rangle_x$ denotes a local coarse-grained density. Equation
(3.3A.1) is the postulate. The remaining identities in this section are its
algebraic consequences.

## Even and odd packages

Define

$$
\mathcal M_k:=\frac{\mathcal J_k^++\mathcal J_k^-}{2},
\qquad
\mathcal P_k:=\mathcal J_k^+-\mathcal J_k^-.
$$

Substitution gives

$$
\boxed{\mathcal M_k=\varrho
:=\left\langle\sum_aM_a\right\rangle_x}
\qquad\text{for every }k,
\tag{3.3A.2}
$$

and

$$
\boxed{\mathcal P_k=j_k
:=\left\langle\sum_a p_{k,a}\right\rangle_x}.
\tag{3.3A.3}
$$

The scalar package is therefore axis-independent without an isotropy
assumption or a $1/3$ share. The odd package is the local net momentum
component. For cold matter at rest, $\mathcal M=\rho c$; for radiation of
energy density $u$, $\mathcal M=u/c$.

The channels are positive carrier by carrier. Since
$|p_k|\leq |\mathbf p|\leq M$,

$$
M\pm\frac12p_k\geq\frac12M\geq0,
$$

so $\mathcal J_k^\pm\geq0$. This positivity is inherited from the declared
shell readings; it is not a separate energy condition.

## The second transport moment

The even and odd packages do not exhaust local momentum transport. Free
carriers also define

$$
\mathcal C_{ij}(x)
:=
\left\langle\sum_a\frac{p_{i,a}p_{j,a}}{M_a}\right\rangle_x.
\tag{3.3A.4}
$$

$\mathcal C_{ij}$ records pressure, counterflow, shear, and radiation
transport. In a local flat bookkeeping frame it enters the first-moment
balance schematically as

$$
\partial_{t_*}\mathcal P_i+c\,\partial_j\mathcal C_{ij}=f_i.
$$

The current minimal stationary field map assigns no independent scalar
response to $\mathcal C_{ij}$. That assignment is part of the adopted source
package; it is not proved by Equation (3.3A.4).

## Free carriers versus interacting systems

Equations (3.3A.2)--(3.3A.4) are exact for the declared local free-carrier
coarse graining. A composite system adds a harder question: how interaction
energy, binding, mediator momentum, wall tension, and improvements are
localized in one conserved M1 ledger. No interaction action presently derives
that allocation.

Classical stationary systems provide a useful comparison. Conservation and
compact support imply the Laue identity

$$
\int T^{ij}\,d^3x=0,
$$

or, axis by axis,

$$
\int T^{ii}\,d^3x=0
\qquad\text{(no sum)}.
\tag{3.3A.5}
$$

Equation (3.3A.5) explains why radiation pressure and confining wall tension
cancel in the exterior monopole of a complete isolated system
[@misner1959active]. It does not derive the corresponding M1 wall and binding
ledger. Nor does it erase local interior differences: the Green kernel weights
different source radii differently even when the unweighted stress integral
vanishes.

## Result

The stationary source construction adopts

$$
\mathcal J_k^\pm
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathcal M=\varrho,
\qquad
\mathcal P_i=j_i,
$$

with channel positivity and axis independence following exactly from SI. The
postulate supplies a clean free-carrier source grammar. It does not yet supply
the interacting allocation needed for walls, binding, or a universal
stress-response law.
